corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 127.0722 mi; paid miles 127 from mileposts: The MILEPOST Seward Highway mileposts; Anchorage–Seward is approximately 126–127 paid miles, represented as 127. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

checkpoints.source: The MILEPOST junction milepost split; approximately 90 paid miles from Anchorage. This is a highway junction, not a city.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 148.0890 mi; paid miles 147 from mileposts: The MILEPOST junction mileposts; Seward Highway to Tern Lake plus Sterling Highway to Soldotna, approximately 90+57=147 paid miles. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 241.2141 mi; paid miles 239 from mileposts: BLM Alaska 2024 Dalton Highway Visitor Guide: Coldfoot MP 175 to Deadhorse MP 414; derived paid miles 414−175=239. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. BLM describes the Dalton as mostly gravel; separate gravel-surface gameplay is not modeled. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

speed_limits.source: Assumed 55 mph where no posted OpenStreetMap maxspeed way lies along the road in Alaska: the unposted default under 13 AAC 02.275.

OpenStreetMap maxspeed tags on the corridor highway ways, read from the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19 and matched within 90 m of a public Valhalla route through the leg's route points; normalized to mph, maxspeed:hgv preferred where tagged.

stops.name: Yukon River Camp
stops.source: Yukon River Camp https://yukonrivercamp.com/ confirms gas and diesel; Dalton MP 56 (BLM 2024 guide), 175−56=119 paid miles south of Coldfoot. Local OSM node 410640133 supports large-vehicle access; parking capacity not verified.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 253.6685 mi; paid miles 259 from mileposts: BLM Alaska 2024 Dalton Highway Visitor Guide: Livengood/Dalton MP 0 is 84 miles north of Fairbanks and Coldfoot is MP 175; derived paid miles 84+175=259. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. BLM describes the Dalton as mostly gravel; separate gravel-surface gameplay is not modeled. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 241.2142 mi; paid miles 239 from mileposts: BLM Alaska 2024 Dalton Highway Visitor Guide: Coldfoot MP 175 to Deadhorse MP 414; derived paid miles 414−175=239. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. BLM describes the Dalton as mostly gravel; separate gravel-surface gameplay is not modeled. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

speed_limits.source: Assumed 55 mph where no posted OpenStreetMap maxspeed way lies along the road in Alaska: the unposted default under 13 AAC 02.275.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 95.4419 mi; paid miles 96 from mileposts: The MILEPOST Richardson Highway mileposts; Delta Junction to Fairbanks is 96 paid miles. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. The split Tok–Delta and Delta–Fairbanks paid-mile total is 204, two miles above the retired 202-mile composite; the residual is preserved, not redistributed. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 150.7879 mi; paid miles 151 from mileposts: The MILEPOST Richardson Highway mileposts, approximately MP 115 at Glennallen to MP 266 at Delta Junction; derived as 266−115=151. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 107.3264 mi; paid miles 108 from mileposts: The MILEPOST Alaska Highway mileposts; Tok to Delta Junction is 108 paid miles. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. The split Tok–Delta and Delta–Fairbanks paid-mile total is 204, two miles above the retired 202-mile composite; the residual is preserved, not redistributed. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 253.6889 mi; paid miles 259 from mileposts: BLM Alaska 2024 Dalton Highway Visitor Guide: Livengood/Dalton MP 0 is 84 miles north of Fairbanks and Coldfoot is MP 175; derived paid miles 84+175=259. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. BLM describes the Dalton as mostly gravel; separate gravel-surface gameplay is not modeled. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 95.0685 mi; paid miles 96 from mileposts: The MILEPOST Richardson Highway mileposts; Delta Junction to Fairbanks is 96 paid miles. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. The split Tok–Delta and Delta–Fairbanks paid-mile total is 204, two miles above the retired 202-mile composite; the residual is preserved, not redistributed. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 150.8913 mi; paid miles 151 from mileposts: The MILEPOST Richardson Highway mileposts, approximately MP 115 at Glennallen to MP 266 at Delta Junction; derived as 266−115=151. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 117.7467 mi; paid miles 115 from mileposts: The MILEPOST Richardson Highway mileposts, MP 0 at Valdez to approximately MP 115 at Glennallen; derived as 115−0=115. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 127.0468 mi; paid miles 127 from mileposts: The MILEPOST Seward Highway mileposts; Anchorage–Seward is approximately 126–127 paid miles, represented as 127. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

speed_limits.source: Assumed 55 mph where no posted OpenStreetMap maxspeed way lies along the road in Alaska: the unposted default under 13 AAC 02.275.

checkpoints.name: Tern Lake junction
checkpoints.source: The MILEPOST Seward Highway MP 37 junction, 37 miles north from Seward; not a city.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 93.7667 mi; paid miles 94 from mileposts: The MILEPOST junction mileposts; Seward Highway MP 0 to Tern Lake MP 37, then approximately 57 miles on Sterling Highway to Soldotna; derived paid miles 37+57=94. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

speed_limits.source: Assumed 55 mph where no posted OpenStreetMap maxspeed way lies along the road in Alaska: the unposted default under 13 AAC 02.275.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 148.0699 mi; paid miles 147 from mileposts: The MILEPOST junction mileposts; Seward Highway to Tern Lake plus Sterling Highway to Soldotna, approximately 90+57=147 paid miles. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 74.7109 mi; paid miles 75 from mileposts: The MILEPOST and Bell's Alaska Highway logs place Homer in town near MP 173, not at the MP 179.5 end of the Spit; Soldotna is around MP 94–96. The city-pin drive is about 75 miles, with router distance recorded separately. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

checkpoints.name: Tern Lake junction
checkpoints.source: Derived from 94 paid miles minus the 37-mile Seward-side segment; not a city.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 93.7567 mi; paid miles 94 from mileposts: The MILEPOST junction mileposts; Seward Highway MP 0 to Tern Lake MP 37, then approximately 57 miles on Sterling Highway to Soldotna; derived paid miles 37+57=94. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 107.5063 mi; paid miles 108 from mileposts: The MILEPOST Alaska Highway mileposts; Tok to Delta Junction is 108 paid miles. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. The split Tok–Delta and Delta–Fairbanks paid-mile total is 204, two miles above the retired 202-mile composite; the residual is preserved, not redistributed. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.
